statement: Find the largest integer $k$ with the following property: whenever real numbers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2024}$ satisfy $x_1^2 = (x_1+x_2)^2 = \cdots = (x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_{2024})^2$, at least $k$ of them are equal.

Given $n \geq 2$ points on a circle, Alice and Bob alternately move a tile from its current position $P$ to some other point $Q$, drawing segment $PQ$ (not allowed if already drawn). Alice starts. A player unable to move loses. Determine, for each $n$, which player has a winning strategy.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$ and circumcenter $O$. Let $D \in AC$ with $AB = AD$. Let $E$ be the intersection of line $AB$ with the perpendicular to $AO$ through $D$. Let $F$ be the intersection of the perpendicular to $OC$ through $C$ with the line parallel to $AC$ through $E$. Let $G = CE \cap DF$. Show that $AG \parallel BF$.
Find all integers $n \geq 2$ for which there exist $n$ integers $a_1, \ldots, a_n \geq 2$ such that for all $i \neq j$, $a_i \mid a_j^2 + 1$.

Let $d$ and $m$ be fixed positive integers. Pinocchio chooses a polynomial $P$ of degree at most $d$ with integer coefficients. Geppetto asks for values $P(n)$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$; Pinocchio may lie up to $m$ times. What is the minimum number of questions Geppetto needs (as a function of $d$ and $m$) to determine $P$?

Given $n \geq 2$, let $P$ and $Q$ be two sets each of $n$ points in 3D space (all $2n$ distinct). Show one can label $P = \{P_1,\ldots,P_n\}$ and $Q = \{Q_1,\ldots,Q_n\}$ so that for any $i,j$, the balls with diameters $P_iQ_i$ and $P_jQ_j$ share at least one common point.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcircle $\omega$ and circumcenter $O$. The altitude from $A$ meets $\omega$ at $D \neq A$; segment $AC$ meets the circumcircle of $\triangle OCD$ at $E \neq C$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BE$. Show that $DE \parallel OM$.
Let $p$ be a fixed prime. Find all integers $n \geq 1$ such that the positive divisors of $n$ can be partitioned into pairs $(d, d')$ with $d < d'$ and $p \mid dd'$.
